description.narrative:
ASCE-LC has applied to Sida for funding of 13 million SEK to carry out the "organisational strengthening project for the high state control and anti-corruption authority of Burkina Faso" in Burkina Faso during the period 2017-2019. The intervention aims at strengthening ASCE-LC's capacities to implement efficiently its mission by 1)facilitating the controllers' mission with strategic and operational documents, 2)the introduction of modern human resources management tools and the improvement of the work conditions to boost the staff motivation; 3)the surveyors and verification assistants master the technics of denunciations reception, survey and report drafting; 4)the state controllers master the internal performance audit technics and the thorough analysis of the financial states of state societies; 5)review the best practices at the peer organisations level; 6)improving the public service of the managers and the senior officers to the users; 7)mastering computerized tools to reinforce ASCE-LC's credibility; 8)increasing the population awareness on corruption issues and agree with the prevention messages; 9)increasing the population ownership of the information and their participation to the actions against corruption; 10)increasing the commitment of the peer partners to the coordination of the fight against corruption; 11)increase citizen reporting of corruption cases to ASCE-LC, and 12)increasing the commitment to fight corruption at all levels. The ASCE-LC will implement the intervention together with CSOs, the general inspection of finances (IGF) and the cour des comptes.
The intervention’s total budget is 13 000 000 millions SEK contributed by Sida.

Den högsta statliga tillsynsmyndigheten för kontroll och anti-korruption, ASCE-LC, har ansökt hos Sida om finansiering med 13 miljoner kronor för genomförande av det organisatoriska kapacitetsstärkande projektet av kontrollmyndigheten i Burkina Faso under perioden 2017-2019.
Insatsen syftar till att förstärka myndighetens allmänna kapacitet för att kontrollera statsförvaltningen och hantera korruptionen i landet genom 1) formulering av strategier 2) personalförstärkning och 3) stärkande av information för att minska korruptionen och förbättra förvaltningen. ASCE-LC kommer att genomföra insatsen tillsammans med det civila samhällets organisationer och Finansinspektionen (Inspection Generale des Finances, IGF) samt Förvaltningsdomstolen (Cours des Comptes).
Insatsens totala budget är 13 000 000 kronor.

" During this 2019 period, the implementation of the project is generally unsatisfactory. Only 37% physical activity completion rate was reported by the project team. The process of revising the logical framework and the Extended action plan of the project led to the late adoption of the work plan only in July 2019. Only 5 months were available for the implementation of this work plan 2019.
In terms of improving the strategic management of the ASCE-LC - The first draft of the national strategy to prevent and fight corruption was developed and validated with the various stakeholders; - 8 specific studies on the state of corruption in eight areas were conducted and finalised to be taken into account in the development of the national strategy to prevent and fight corruption and related offences. - A Strategic Plan (SP) for 2025 of the ASCE-LC was developed and adopted - Two investigation and verification guides have been designed with the technical support of magistrates and implemented - Training sessions on service management, interpersonal and media communication, and team management and leadership were held for heads of department, state auditors and ASCE-LC directors and heads of service - An in-depth training workshop on Excel software was conducted for all state auditors - An ASCE-LC gender strategy with an action plan was adopted in March 2021 - A study trip to the OFNAC in Senegal was carried out to improve cooperation with countries in the sub-region in the fight against corruption.
In terms of strengthening the control profession - An updated manual of procedures for receiving, analysing and processing whistleblowers and a scoreboard of complaints and whistleblowers has been put in place; - An electronic system for monitoring the implementation of recommendations and legal actions has been designed and is operational - A manual of procedures and a dashboard for monitoring indicators integrating computerisation of declarations of interest and assets has been designed Gender budget formulation and control tools are designed and applied by the ASCE-LC at internal and external levels; - The investigation department is equipped with database software and specific investigation materials; - The capacities of the staff of the audit and control department are strengthened through a series of training and coaching sessions on risk management and fraud management and through study tours; - Training sessions on the methodology for drawing up the minutes of investigation hearings and techniques for drafting standard reports carried out ; - Training sessions on the in-depth analysis of financial statements of state-owned companies carried out State auditors trained in gender analysis of budgets to detect elements that reduce inequalities Coaching on the application of gender budgeting training for the benefit of those trained; - The reinforcement of the ASCE-LC's fleet of vehicles through the acquisition of four (4) vehicles to facilitate control and anti-corruption missions. - The acquisition of thirty-six (36) briefcases for state auditors. The cases, which include laptops, telephones, recorders, scanners, etc., will enable the State auditors to better conduct their missions.
In terms of communication and prevention: - The strategy for popularising Law No. 04-2015/CNT on the prevention and repression of corruption is being implemented through awareness campaigns programmed with the support of the United Nations Development Programme, other awareness campaigns have been carried out. A hundred or so communes in the Centre-East, Boucle du Mouhoun, Hauts Bassins, Cascades, South-West and Central Plateau regions have benefited from these awareness campaigns. - Educational conferences are organised and conducted in 25 secondary schools in the Centre-West, Boucle du Mouhoun, Hauts Bassins and Plateau Central regions. - A documentary film on corruption produced in 2020 and broadcast this year 2021 on four television channels: 3TV, TNB, Burkina info and BF1.
In terms of coordination and consultation with other actors : - Draft regulations for consultation between the three control bodies (ASCE/LC, Cour des Comptes, IGF) were drawn up and validated - Some civil society actors, REN-LAC and LEJEPAD, have been supported in popularising anti-corruption messages. RENLAC organised a day of questioning of the government. As for LEJEPAD, it carried out various awareness-raising activities (radio programmes, public events, etc.) in Bobo-Dioulasso (Hauts-Bassins) and Banfora (Cascades).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
